summary: OpenAI released two updated Realtime API models, gpt-realtime-2.1 and gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, with improved caching-based latency reduction, updated voice-agent behavior, and published pricing.

mechanisms.reason: The post states a caching improvement reduced p95 latency across Realtime voice models by at least 25%, a serving-side efficiency gain.
mechanisms.quote: we’ve also reduced p95 latency by at least 25% across Realtime voice models through improved caching

practices.reason: The updated model claims improved instruction following, tool use, and interruption/noise handling, relevant to voice-agent teams evaluating an upgrade.
practices.quote: gpt-realtime-2.1 updates GPT-Realtime-2 with improved alphanumeric recognition, silence and noise handling, and interruption behavior.

practices.reason: The stated latency reduction comes from OpenAI's own caching implementation on their serving stack, not a technique we could directly apply.
practices.quote: we’ve also reduced p95 latency by at least 25% across Realtime voice models through improved caching

practices.reason: New model versions with a distinct pricing table mean teams choosing between them must update model selection logic and cost estimates.
practices.quote: Use gpt-realtime-2.1 when you want the strongest realtime reasoning, tool use, instruction following, and voice-agent behavior. Use gpt-realtime-2.1-mini when you want a faster, more cost-efficient option for realtime voice experiences.
